top_stories.title: Alberta Referendum: Voters Reject Separation from Canada
points: 76% of over 1.5M votes counted favored staying in Canada; 24% supported beginning separation process.

issues.subject: 🔔Opening Bell Daily: Chips snap rare streak

headlines: Semiconductor stocks rebounded after 8 consecutive trading days of losses, snapping their longest losing streak since October 2008, though historical patterns suggest caution ahead.
Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) rose 1.6% Monday but gave back gains intraday, still sitting 22.7% below its June record high.
After previous 8+ day losing streaks in the SOX since 1994, the median one-month return was -5.2% (versus +1.8% for any random month), suggesting bounces may not signal sustained recovery.
Wholesale prices jumped 6.3% year-over-year in September—the biggest increase since 2022—keeping Fed rate cut odds low ahead of October 28 decision.
Apple scheduled October 28 launch event expected to feature a touchscreen laptop as tech earnings season kicks off this week.

sections.title: The Semiconductor Losing Streak and What History Shows
points: The SOX fell for 8 straight trading sessions, matching only one other occurrence since October 2008; chip ETFs SMH and SOXX actually fell 9 days in a row.
Since 1994, the SOX has experienced 8+ day losing streaks just 8 times total—two reached 9 days, none reached 10.
After all 7 prior occurrences: the SOX bounced the next day (median gain 1.4%), but 5 of 7 were lower one month later (median return -5.2%, well below the +1.8% average for any given month).
Six-month outlook after similar streaks: median gain was only 2%, versus 9.8% for any typical 6-month period, indicating prolonged underperformance.

sections.title: Breadth and Technicals
points: Monday's rebound appeared broad-based: 26 of the SOX's 30 stocks finished higher, suggesting participation beyond a few names.
The SOX rose 3.7% at its intraday high but gave back more than half those gains, closing below where it opened—a sign of weakness despite the positive session.
The index remains deeply underwater: down 22.7% from its June peak as of Monday's close.

sections.title: Macro and Market Catalysts
points: 10-year Treasury yield holding above 5%; wholesale price inflation at 6.3% year-over-year (September) is the biggest jump since 2022.
Traders pricing in above-80% probability the Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady at October 28 decision, suggesting inflation concerns are not yet triggering cuts.
Heavy week of tech earnings kicks off this week, which could influence semiconductor and broader market direction.
